answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days and the line running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, any option requiring onboarding or dual-qualification (switch_primary_vendor, add_second_source) carries unacceptable near-term delivery risk given the timeline. Deferring is also unattractive since finance has mandated an 18% spend cut this year and the contract does not auto-renew, so inaction forfeits leverage. memory_c4 indicates that renegotiating at renewal, benchmarked against market rates, previously recovered real margin and improved payment terms without disrupting supply, and memory_c1 shows incumbent renewal has historically preserved integration stability and delivery continuity. I verified c4 and c2 to confirm whether the low-cost vendor switch record (c2) offers a materially better cost outcome than negotiation before committing, since that is the main competing lever for hitting the 18% target. Pending that check, negotiate_terms is the action most likely to reduce TCO while holding delivery risk flat, and it directly addresses the imminent contract expiration. Other directions (switch, second-source, defer) are preserved as open options for the next review cycle rather than ruled out permanently.
